Data: [Housing Finance Agency Portfolio](https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/housing-finance-agency-portfolio), published by the DC Housing Finance Agency via Data.gov. Licence: [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

The goal of this analysis was to find out how many properties each management company manages per ward in Washington, DC.

```{python}
#reading in the data
import pandas as pd 
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

housing = pd.read_csv("Housing_finance.csv")
housing.head()

#removing houses that do not have a management company
housing.dropna(subset=["Management Company"])

#pivot: for each management company, how many properties does it manage per ward
pivot = housing.pivot_table(index='Management Company', columns='Ward', values='Units').fillna(0)
pivot.max(axis = 1)

#most properties managed per company
top_ward = pd.DataFrame({
    "Top Ward": pivot.idxmax(axis=1),
    "Properties": pivot.max(axis=1),
}).sort_values("Properties", ascending=False)
top_ward.head(10)
```

Steps I took:
First, I read in the data with pandas
Next, I removed the properties that do not have a management company
Then I created a pivot table that counts how many properties each company manages in each ward.
Finally, I found the ward where each company manages the most properties
